questions.stem: The essential approximation of Weiss mean-field theory is to:

options.A: solve the model exactly on a lattice
options.C: replace interactions of a spin with its neighbours by an average (molecular) field proportional to the magnetization

explanation.whyCorrect: \(H_{eff} = -(zJ\langle s\rangle + h)s_i\): fluctuations of neighbours about their mean are neglected.

whyWrong.B: Then there would be no ordering.
whyWrong.D: Mean field can be applied to quantum spins too.

explanation.howToAvoid: Mean field = average neighbours, neglect fluctuations.

questions.stem: In mean-field theory of the Ising model \(H = -J\sum_{\langle ij\rangle}s_is_j\) (\(s=\pm1\)) on a square lattice (\(z = 4\)), the critical temperature is:

explanation.whyCorrect: Self-consistency \(m = \tanh(\beta zJm)\) has a non-zero solution when \(\beta zJ > 1\): \(k_BT_c = zJ = 4J\). (Exact: 2.27J — mean field overestimates.)

whyWrong.A: Onsager's exact value, not mean field.

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the mean-field \(T_c\) on a simple cubic lattice (6J).

questions.stem: Above \(T_c\), mean-field theory predicts the magnetic susceptibility follows:

explanation.whyCorrect: Curie–Weiss law \(\chi = C/(T-T_c)\), diverging at \(T_c\) (exponent γ = 1).
explanation.howToAvoid: Interactions shift the divergence from 0 to \(T_c\).

questions.stem: Mean-field theory becomes exact (or most accurate) for:

options.B: systems with very many neighbours or long-range interactions (high dimensions)

explanation.whyCorrect: Averaging over many neighbours suppresses relative fluctuations; above the upper critical dimension (4 for Ising) mean-field exponents are exact.

whyWrong.A: Worst case: it wrongly predicts a transition in 1D.
whyWrong.C: Accuracy depends on fluctuations near \(T_c\), not on T → 0.

explanation.howToModify: Ask for the upper critical dimension of the Ising model (4).
explanation.howToAvoid: More neighbours → better averaging → better mean field.

questions.stem: With Landau free energy \(F(m) = a(T-T_c)m^2 + bm^4\) (\(a,b>0\)), the equilibrium magnetization below \(T_c\) is:

whyWrong.B: That is a maximum of \(F\) below \(T_c\).

explanation.trapUsed: Choosing the stationary point that is a maximum.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the free-energy difference \(\Delta F\) below \(T_c\) and the heat-capacity jump.
explanation.howToAvoid: Check the second derivative to confirm a minimum.

questions.stem: Applied to the 1D Ising chain, mean-field theory:

explanation.whyCorrect: With \(z = 2\), mean field gives \(k_BT_c = 2J\), whereas the exact solution has no transition at \(T>0\): fluctuations dominate in low dimensions.

whyWrong.A: Mean field gives a continuous transition.
whyWrong.B: It can be applied, just inaccurately.
whyWrong.C: Exact answer, not the mean-field one.

explanation.conceptTested: Failure of mean field in low dimensions
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the lower critical dimension of the Ising model (1).
explanation.howToAvoid: Mean field always predicts order when \(zJ > 0\).
